### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via NO_EXECUTOR (literal, a string literal in executeNode))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db1a05cdaeec179bdf327c1e357ac7bbc6b678b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c7bfdd1c46daaacbf0dcbd51125a02aaed027bc9` — the merge of head `bdee8dcff8b615f1a1e63bdba2269210b73f8f66` into base `db1a05cdaeec179bdf327c1e357ac7bbc6b678b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c7bfdd1c46daaacbf0dcbd51125a02aaed027bc9 && git checkout c7bfdd1c46daaacbf0dcbd51125a02aaed027bc9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin db1a05cdaeec179bdf327c1e357ac7bbc6b678b9 bdee8dcff8b615f1a1e63bdba2269210b73f8f66 && git checkout -B drift-repro db1a05cdaeec179bdf327c1e357ac7bbc6b678b9 && git merge --no-ff bdee8dcff8b615f1a1e63bdba2269210b73f8f66

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db1a05cdaeec179bdf327c1e357ac7bbc6b678b9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs db1a05cdaeec179bdf327c1e357ac7bbc6b678b9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T21:54Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `bdee8dcff8b615f1a1e63bdba2269210b73f8f66`

Read against claim 6960587921 (route 1) and card #34959. The change is 4 files, +270/-22, and `check-governed-merges --branch` says it is not governed. Every file sits inside the claim surface: `dag-traversal.ts`, two of its test files (new top-level describes only, with no existing assertion edited), and a changeset.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- **The `followFaultEdge` extraction is behaviour-preserving.**
  - Both old arms did the same three things: find the `fault` edge, find its target, then `this.executeNode` and return. The helper does exactly that and answers `false` in the same two cases, no edge or a dangling target, so the caller then throws as before.
  - The may-route decision stays at each call site and is unchanged: `!isGuardRefusal(execErr)` on the throw arm and `errorClass !== 'guard'` on the returned arm. The `&&` short-circuit means a guard refusal never looks up the edge, the same as the old `? undefined`.
  - `host.executeNode(...)` is called as a method on `this`, so the binding is the same.
  - Your reason for not throwing a coded error inside the `try` holds. The catch would record `EXECUTION_ERROR`, publish `$error` without `code`, and run the `readPartialSteps` fold for a node that never ran.
- **Point (2): `$error.code: NO_EXECUTOR` with no fault edge fits route 1. No amendment is needed.**
  - The card's Expected 1 says the failure is "graded like any other node failure … (and `$error.code` reads `NO_EXECUTOR`)". Publish-before-route (#14955) is how every other failure arm grades, so publishing on the no-edge path is that rule applied, not a new behaviour.
  - The only runtime reader of `$error` in service-automation and plugins is `try-catch-node.ts` (lines 189 and 245). Its identity guard (`innerError !== errorBefore`) means it used to bind no code for this failure, and now binds `NO_EXECUTOR`. This is the same as a returned failure with a classified code.
  - `NO_EXECUTOR` is already a ledgered code (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts`), and `lastErrorCode` is a plain `string`, so no enum is widened.
  - The change is pinned in `throw-arm-error-refresh.test.ts` and disclosed in both the changeset and the body.
- **No privilege angle in routing it.** The node never ran, so no guard is skipped. The handler runs only because the author declared the edge, and the author could have written that path directly. Treating it as `runtime` rather than `guard` is consistent with the boot audit only warning (ADR-0018).
- **The controls pin the unchanged arms.** With no fault edge, the failure keeps the same step, byte-identical text and `failed`. `start` with no executor still succeeds and leaves `$error` untouched. A registered executor that throws still records `EXECUTION_ERROR` with no `code`. The reported ablation (base blob for `dag-traversal.ts`, hash-checked set and restore) turns exactly the 3 new routing and publishing tests red, and all 4 controls stay green.
- **Point (3), out of scope and fine to leave:**
  - The `engine.ts` ~5645 comment ("throws NO_EXECUTOR") is now loose. It is a comment outside the surface; whoever next touches that file can fix it.
  - The `executeNode` docblock's "moved unedited" is now historical only.
  - The retry re-runs (the `try_catch` ladder and flow `errorHandling: retry`) are pre-existing and bounded.
  - Dry-run follows the fault edge through the shared arm, which is not pinned separately. None of these needs a card from this review.

Landing: not governed. CI on this exact head was still running when I read it (12 success, 16 skipped, 22 in progress). Area o3-G lands it once it is fully green. A later push owes a delta read.
